Historically, LD50 tests were conducted by administering different doses of a substance to multiple groups of animals – typically mice, rats, rabbits, or guinea pigs – and observing the effects. Researchers would record the dose that caused mortality in 50% of the animals in each group. The LD50 value is then calculated from this data. The animals are observed for a period of 14 days to assess mortality.

The OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) has developed numerous test guidelines for alternative methods.

Regulations regarding LD50 testing vary by country and region. Many countries have implemented restrictions or outright bans on LD50 testing for certain products, such as cosmetics.
